cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Approve the Cover Story
cards.instruction: Get someone to endorse an explanation that protects the plan, reputation, or people involved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've approved 'delivery delay' for the newsletter. Put your name with mine; the new volunteer mustn't take the blame for the melted cake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we be accurate? She was on time. We left it by the radiator.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Accuracy is authorized. 'Storage problem.' You may support that wording.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll sign if we mention the refund.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Condition accepted. 'Storage problem; full refund arranged.' Your signature may follow mine. I want both of us standing behind the volunteer.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 authorizes accuracy as A's concession and A5 grants the refund condition while directing signature order to secure public support.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 corrects delivery to storage, used in A3; B4 refund condition is incorporated in A5.

relationship.evidence: B2 refuses false blame and B4 makes endorsement conditional on remedy, so B has agency.

heightening.evidence: A5 adds refund and joint names because B4 will sign only on that condition.

specificity.evidence: A1 newsletter and volunteer blame plus B2 radiator establish the reputational problem.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 signature following mine reveals rank; the protective closing is sincere but not highly witty.
